item.title: Java SDK
item.description: The Java SDK needs Java 17 or later and has no runtime dependencies. Package: io.speedle:speedle-sdk 0.2.0 on Maven Central. Reference: speedle-sdk/java. The examples check the policy described in the SDKs overview. Add the dependency Maven, a complete pom.xml: <?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?> <project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance" xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 https://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd"> <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion> <groupId>com.example</groupId> <artifactId>speedle-example</artifactId> <version>1.0</version> <properties> <maven.compiler.release>17</maven.compiler.release> <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding> </properties> <dependencies> <dependency> <groupId>io.speedle</groupId> <artifactId>speedle-sdk</artifactId> <version>0.2.0</version> </dependency> </dependencies> </project> Gradle, a complete build.gradle.kts (with a settings.gradle.kts that sets rootProject.

item.title: Python SDK
item.description: The Python SDK needs Python 3.10 or later; its only runtime dependency is httpx. It has a sync Client and an asyncio AsyncClient with the same arguments. Package: speedle 0.2.0 on PyPI. Reference: speedle-sdk/python. The examples check the policy described in the SDKs overview. Add the dependency With pip, in a virtual environment: python3 -m venv .venv . .venv/bin/activate pip install speedle==0.2.0 Or with uv, in a uv project:

item.title: Go SDK
item.description: The Go SDK supports the two latest Go releases and uses only the standard library. Module: github.com/teramoby/speedle-sdk/go v0.2.0, package speedle. Reference: speedle-sdk/go. The examples check the policy described in the SDKs overview. Add the dependency In a new module: go mod init example.com/speedle-example go get github.com/teramoby/speedle-sdk/go@v0.2.0 Call a local Speedle Start Speedle and create the example policy as described in the SDKs overview. Save this program as main.go: package main import ( "context" "fmt" "os" speedle "github.

item.title: C#/.NET SDK
item.description: The .NET SDK targets .NET 8 or later and has no dependencies. Package: Speedle.Sdk 0.2.0 on NuGet, namespace Speedle.Sdk. Reference: speedle-sdk/dotnet. The examples check the policy described in the SDKs overview. Add the dependency In a new console project: dotnet new console -o SpeedleExample cd SpeedleExample dotnet add package Speedle.Sdk --version 0.2.0 Call a local Speedle Start Speedle and create the example policy as described in the SDKs overview. Replace Program.

item.title: Rust SDK
item.description: The Rust SDK needs Rust 1.75 or later. It is async on tokio and reqwest (rustls); the blocking feature adds the blocking client used below. Crate: speedle 0.2.0 on crates.io. Reference: speedle-sdk/rust. The examples check the policy described in the SDKs overview. Add the dependency In a new package: cargo new speedle-example cd speedle-example cargo add speedle@0.2.0 --features blocking Call a local Speedle Start Speedle and create the example policy as described in the SDKs overview.

item.title: Node.js/TypeScript SDK
item.description: The Node.js SDK needs Node.js 22 or later, ships ESM and CommonJS builds with TypeScript types, and has no runtime dependencies. Package: @speedle/sdk, published on npm. Reference: speedle-sdk/node. The examples check the policy described in the SDKs overview. Add the dependency In a new ES module package: mkdir speedle-example cd speedle-example npm init -y npm pkg set type=module npm install @speedle/sdk@0.2.1 Call a local Speedle Start Speedle and create the example policy as described in the SDKs overview.

item.title: Docker image
item.description: Speedle publishes one image that contains speedle-pms, speedle-ads and spctl. The image is built FROM scratch, runs as UID 65532, and has no shell. The first argument selects the program. The same image index is on both registries: Docker Hub: docker.io/speedle/speedle GHCR: ghcr.io/teramoby/speedle Release 1.7.0 publishes the tags 1.7.0, 1.7 and latest on both registries, for linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. Pull the image docker pull docker.io/speedle/speedle:1.7.0 docker pull ghcr.
